issues.issue_title: Ethernet: CRCStripTypePacket does not work Stm32H7S3L8 NUCLEO
issues.st_ready_text:
Problem: Ethernet: CRCStripTypePacket does not work Stm32H7S3L8 NUCLEO
Context: repo=stm32h7rsxx-hal-driver, mcu_series=H7, board=STM32H7S3L8, component=ETH, layer=Other, issue_kind=bug_report, severity=high, evidence_strength=high, rescue_applied=False, state=closed, issue_number=10
Root cause: Hello @FullDevStudio, Thank you for your report.
Fix: Hello everyone, I have the following use case: I want to receive raw data via Ethernet, which works fine, but I have a problem: When I send 100 bytes, I only receive 14 bytes in my software on the MCU (STM32H7S3L8).
Constraints: Validate against exact MCU/board configuration and CubeMX/CubeH7 version before applying.
Keywords: H7, STM32H7S3L8, ETH, bug_report, high, question, hal, internal bug tracker, st community, MCU, DISABLE, CRC

Technical details:
Hello everyone, I have the following use case: I want to receive raw data via Ethernet, which works fine, but I have a problem: When I send 100 bytes, I only receive 14 bytes in my software on the MCU (STM32H7S3L8). I was able to fix this by setting AutomaticPadCRCStrip to DISABLE. Now I receive 104 bytes, which is also not the desired behavior. After a little research, I found out that the 4 bytes are CRC, so I continued searching. After some searching, I found the CRCStripTypePacket property and set it to ENABLE, but unfortunately this property has no effect. What do I need to do to get my 100 bytes but not the CRC? Do I need to set something else? Is this a bug? Please help me, I'm stuck. Legitimate Ethernet frames work, but I want to use my own protocol without the Ethernet header in front of it. I am asking for help with the setup so that my data arrives as it was sent. Here is a link to the stm32 forum where I already asked the question. https://community.st.com/t5/stm32-mcus-embedded-software/raw-ethernet-how-can-i-remove-the-crc-upon-receipt/m-p/863127#M70863 Thank you very much, stm32h7rsxx-hal-driver 1.2.1

Key comments:
Hello @FullDevStudio, Thank you for your report. This issue has been tracked internally. ST Internal Reference: 224306 Hello @FullDevStudio, We will continue tracking this issue on the ST Community post: https://community.st.com/t5/stm32-mcus-embedded-software/raw-ethernet-how-can-i-remove-the-crc-upon-receipt/m-p/863127#M70863. Therefore, please allow me to close this ticket on GitHub. Rest assured, the issue is being tracked internally, and we will keep you updated on any progress.

issues.issue_title: SDIO HAL ReadExtended / WriteExtended does not calculate number of blocks correctly
issues.st_ready_text:
Problem: SDIO HAL ReadExtended / WriteExtended does not calculate number of blocks correctly
Context: repo=stm32h7rsxx-hal-driver, mcu_series=H7, board=STM32H7RSXX, component=None, layer=HAL, issue_kind=bug_report, severity=high, evidence_strength=high, rescue_applied=True, state=closed, issue_number=9
Root cause: On a second thought I may be in the wrong about supporting writing / reading of data that's not multiple of block size in block mode.
Fix: The HAL driver in functions HAL_SDIO_ReadExtended() and HAL_SDIO_WriteExtended() does not calculate number of blocks to read / write correctly.
Constraints: Validate against exact MCU/board configuration and CubeMX/CubeH7 version before applying.
Keywords: H7, STM32H7RSXX, HAL, bug_report, high, bug, invalid, sdmmc, HAL_SDIO_ReadExtended, HAL_SDIO_WriteExtended, Size_byte, block_size

Technical details:
The HAL driver in functions HAL_SDIO_ReadExtended() and HAL_SDIO_WriteExtended() does not calculate number of blocks to read / write correctly. The code in question is: https://github.com/STMicroelectronics/stm32h7rsxx-hal-driver/blob/580b47200c8d757a72ecfc38abb59f9db7041a29/Src/stm32h7rsxx_hal_sdio.c#L976 The same code is used in other read / write functions. The calculated block number will only be correct for the case size == block size. It should be possible to send data with different length than multiple of block size (I haven't seen any limitation noted in that regard). Here are a few example results of calculating number of blocks with this code: - Size_byte=512, hsdio->block_size=512 -> nbr_of_block=1 : OK - Size_byte=510, hsdio->block_size=512 -> nbr_of_block=0 : NOT OK, expected 1 - Size_byte=513, hsdio->block_size=512 -> nbr_of_block=1 : NOT OK, expected 2 - Size_byte=2048, hsdio->block_size=512 -> nbr_of_block=4 : OK - Size_byte=2049, hsdio->block_size=512 -> nbr_of_block=4 : NOT_OK, expected 5 We can see that the calculated size is true only when size_byte is a multiple of hsdio->block_size=512, otherwise the calculated number of blocks is 1 block to small. Example of correct calculation of block size: /* Assuming block mode, minimum 1-block to send */ nbr_of_blocks = 1; while(Size_byte > hsdio->block_size) { nbr_of_blocks++; Size_byte -= hsdio->block_size; }

Key comments:
On a second thought I may be in the wrong about supporting writing / reading of data that's not multiple of block size in block mode. I think if there is no hardware or SDMMC LL driver limitation it's a valid use case. That would allow to send data payloads larger than 512 bytes (limitation of byte mode) without allocating extra large buffers in the application). But I think there may be more changes need in order to make that work, for example adjusting this: https://github.com/STMicroelectronics/stm32h7rsxx-hal-driver/blob/580b47200c8d757a72ecfc38abb59f9db7041a29/Src/stm32h7rsxx_hal_sdio.c#L994 Hello @MaroMetelski, Thank you for your report. After analyzing the issue and returning to the STM32H7 reference manual [RM0477](https://www.st.com/resource/en/reference_manual/rm0477-stm32h7rx7sx-armbased-32bit-mcus-stmicroelectronics.pdf) we found that this behavior is expected. In the RM at SDMMC registers section, the description of the SDMMC data length register (SDMMC_DLENR) this register contains the number of data bytes to be transferred, Regarding the bits descriptions: > When DDR = 1 DATALENGTH is truncated to a multiple of 2. (The last odd byte is not transferred) > Note: Fo

Root cause: Hello @MedFedi, Thank you for your report.
Fix: Hello, Setup : STM32 NUCLEO-H7S3L8 NUCLEO .
Constraints: Validate against exact MCU/board configuration and CubeMX/CubeH7 version before applying.
Keywords: H7, NUCLEO-H7S3L8, HAL, bug_report, low, documentation, enhancement, internal bug tracker, gpio, STM32, NUCLEO, ODR

Technical details:
Hello, Setup : STM32 NUCLEO-H7S3L8 NUCLEO . Observed symptom : I encountered a problem while deinitializing the GPIO. The ODR register does not return to its reset value. In this example, I'm trying to reset the state of PA10, but some registers, like ODR, do not return to their reset value. I also tried PB7 and had the same problem. Expected behavior : The ODR must return to its reset value. Here you found a screenshot for the issue : ![Image](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/9a8876bd-20b9-4bbb-a64e-b8a3b7a6a946) Best regards, Lafi Mohamed Fedi

Key comments:
Hello @MedFedi, Thank you for your report. The scope of the HAL_GPIO_DeInit() API is limited to resetting the configuration registers. Therefore, the issue is not with the functionality of the API itself but rather with its description. This will be fixed soon. ST Internal Reference: 208308 Hello @TOUNSTM , Thank you for your reply. In the STM32H743, when I use the HAL_GPIO_DeInit() function, the ODR (Output Data Register) returns to its reset value. I need the same behavior for the STM32H7S3L8. By the way, the HAL_GPIO_Init() function in the STM32H743 and the STM32H7S3L8 does not initialize the ODR register. LAFI Mohamed Fedi Hello @TOUNSTM , Thank you for your reply. The comments were confusing to me. I thought that the ODR register was supposed to return to its reset value. LAFI Mohamed Fedi Fixed in 68e6cb59339fec2b0dd1c90f1492c39d18e69af7

Problem: Overflow when transmitting SPI data
Context: repo=stm32h7rsxx-hal-driver, mcu_series=H7, board=STM32H7S7I8, component=None, layer=HAL, issue_kind=bug_report, severity=medium, evidence_strength=high, rescue_applied=False, state=closed, issue_number=6
Root cause: We work with the STM32H7S7I8 running at a SYSCLK of 600Mhz.
Fix: HAL_SPI_TransmitReceive gives a timeout in polling mode.
Constraints: Validate against exact MCU/board configuration and CubeMX/CubeH7 version before applying.
Keywords: H7, STM32H7S7I8, HAL, bug_report, medium, bug, spi, HAL_SPI_TransmitReceive, SPI5, SPI_FLAG_RXP, SPI_CloseTransfer, SPI_FLAG_OVR

Technical details:
HAL_SPI_TransmitReceive gives a timeout in polling mode. When transmitting over SPI5 we get a timeout on transmitting upon sending a large dataset (4096 bytes). SPI5 is configured as a Master, 2 Line device, transmit and receive data in 8 Bit mode. Not in every loop the SPI_FLAG_RXP is set, so no data is read. This will cause a discrepancy in the TxXferCount and RxXferCount and therefor a Timeout after the /* Timeout management */ When setting a breakpoint on the corresponding SPI_CloseTransfer we also see SPI_FLAG_OVR is set. However when checking for the SPI_FLAG_OVR in the loop, this is never set and will transmit all bytes successfully. A tiny delay might seem to be the solution. Since the function is polling, a wait for SPI_FLAG_TXP might be a solution Clock settings: ![Image](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/1cb4e210-7b37-43a1-98ef-aea451065fd3) ![Image](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/26590aa5-843e-4c20-a185-fdf0fc121bc3)

Key comments:
We work with the STM32H7S7I8 running at a SYSCLK of 600Mhz. The code is running from external RAM bus speed 100MHz, DTR enabled - 8 bit wide ICache as well as DCache is enabled We initialize the SPI 5 peripheral as follows: Peripheral clock 150MHz BaudRatePrescaler 2 (SPI master clock/8 so outgoing clock @ ~19MHz) SPI_MODE_MASTER; // Set the mode to SPI master SPI_DIRECTION_2LINES; // Set the mode to 2 lines full duplex SPI_DATASIZE_8BIT; // Set the data size to 8 bit It might be that the peripheral is too fast for the external code to load? I will run a test with the peripheral clock at a lower speed HI @rgqsch, I think so, I will try to find out more and keep you posted. Hello @rgqsch, I checked with our team, and if you are sure about The code is running from external RAM bus speed 100MHz, they recommend that the speed of the external RAM should be higher than the clock of the peripheral (it can be up to 2 times). With regards @KRASTM Thanks for the reply. Just to be clear: we run the code from XSPI2 @100MHz in Memory Mapped Mode. But communicating to another peripheral on SPI5. I will try reducing the SPI5 clock, and check if that will work Edit: After setting the APB

Problem: Error transmitting SPI-Master Full Duplex
Context: repo=stm32h7rsxx-hal-driver, mcu_series=H7, board=None, component=None, layer=HAL, issue_kind=bug_report, severity=medium, evidence_strength=high, rescue_applied=True, state=closed, issue_number=5
Root cause: Hello @rgqsch, Thank you for the report.
Fix: When receiving in SPI Master, full duplex mode using HAL_StatusTypeDef HAL_SPI_Receive(SPI_HandleTypeDef *hspi, uint8_t *pData, uint16_t Size, uint32_t Timeout) if ((hspi->Init.
Constraints: Validate against exact MCU/board configuration and CubeMX/CubeH7 version before applying.
Keywords: H7, HAL, bug_report, medium, bug, duplicate, spi, HAL_StatusTypeDef, HAL_SPI_Receive, SPI_HandleTypeDef, SPI_MODE_MASTER, SPI_DIRECTION_2LINES

Technical details:
When receiving in SPI Master, full duplex mode using HAL_StatusTypeDef HAL_SPI_Receive(SPI_HandleTypeDef *hspi, uint8_t *pData, uint16_t Size, uint32_t Timeout) if ((hspi->Init.Mode == SPI_MODE_MASTER) && (hspi->Init.Direction == SPI_DIRECTION_2LINES)) { hspi->State = HAL_SPI_STATE_BUSY_RX; /* Call transmit-receive function to send Dummy data on Tx line and generate clock on CLK line */ return HAL_SPI_TransmitReceive(hspi, pData, pData, Size, Timeout); } In the H7rsxx library, this check is removed. When manually adding this check the code will run as intended We mainly notice these errors at larger messages (7+ bytes), or smaller prescaler (16-)

Key comments:
Hello @rgqsch, Thank you for the report. Could you please, provide us with more details such as your config especially which instance and the clock you are using, or is it the same for this issue #6. In the meantime, I will try to run some tests. As for the snippet code you mentioned, I have checked with our team and there is no reason to keep it anymore especially for the new series. Thanks, Yes the same clock settings are used as in the other report The provided snippet can of course be added to our own code More information: SPI5 - 150MHz Baudrate 30MHz BaudRatePrescaler 2 (SPI master clock/8) SPI_MODE_MASTER; // Set the mode to SPI master SPI_DIRECTION_2LINES; // Set the mode to 2 lines full duplex SPI_DATASIZE_8BIT; // Set the data size to 8 bit If you need any more information please ask. Thank you @rgqsch. Please, more details on the error and I propose to link the 2 issues. Sure, For this error is possible to work around in our own code, and may be closed I propose to continue on the other thread, that one seems to have impact on the communication and might be more stringen

Technical details:
Hello, The file stm32h7rsxx_util_i3c.c does not have the #ifdef HAL_I3C_MODULE_ENABLED that the other HAL components have, which leads to undefined symbols when we compile with I3C module disabled. Same goes for its corresponding header file if we add the ifdef in the stm32h7rsxx_util_i3c.c file after the include (it seems to be done that way in the other sources).

The #ifdef HAL_xxx_MODULE_ENABLED used in all HAL component, but the file stm32h7rsxx_util_i3c.c it is a helper that contain 2 functions for computation of different timing parameter as mentioned in the brief at the top of the file **"This utility help to calculate the different I3C Timing"**. In other word an extra file could be included when needed, if I3C module used and enabled, with HAL_DRIVER or FULL_LL_DRIVER.
